text:
## Screening summary: Cap des Biches, Rufisque, Dakar region, Senegal (thermal)

The point sits on the Cap des Biches power complex, on the coast east of Rufisque in the Dakar metropolitan periphery. OSM and Wikidata both place existing thermal plant on or within metres of the point, including a substation, a combined-cycle plant, and gas or oil units. Any new thermal asset here would be an expansion of an existing industrial cluster, not a greenfield site. Residential land and a place of worship are mapped at or within the 0.5 km footprint edge, which makes the site a dense urban and peri-urban setting.

**PS5 (land and resettlement): triggered, high.** Two residential polygons touch the footprint edge, and informal settlements are mapped about 2 km away. Rufisque (about 2.7 km) and Mbao (about 2.9 km) are close. Land tenure is unknown from these data. Informal occupation is under-mapped, so the absence of further features is not evidence of absence. The rating depends on whether the project needs land beyond the existing industrial parcel, and on any access road that would cross settled areas.

**PS6 (biodiversity and ecosystem services): triggered, medium.** GBIF holds 43 records of six Critically Endangered or Endangered species within 5 km. The nearest is the Hooded Vulture (CR, 23 records, latest 2025, about 2.3 km). Other records include a CR guitarfish (*Rhinobatos rhinobatos*, mostly 1981) and an EN tortoise (*Centrochelys sulcata*, 2018). Nineteen OSM wetlands lie within 5 km, the nearest about 3.3 km, and a Wikidata wetland, the Niaye de Thiaroye, lies about 4.6 km away. A river is mapped about 2.1 km away. No Ramsar site or formal protected area lies within 5 km; the nearest protected area is about 6.7 km. Vultures are a particular concern for thermal assets because of collision and electrocution risk from new lines and structures. The coastal and wetland habitats also raise hydrological and emissions questions. Records are sightings and do not show ranges.

**PS4 (community health, safety and security): triggered, medium.** About 100 schools and health facilities lie within 5 km, and one school is about 0.7 km away. The existing plants already create traffic, noise and emissions exposure. Trunk roads are within 0.35 km, so construction traffic will be a near-field issue. Cumulative exposure with the nearby Kounoune oil-fired station (about 4 km) should be assessed.

**PS7 (Indigenous Peoples): not triggered, low.** No Indigenous or community land is mapped within 20 km. This is a screen result only; it does not rule out customary or community tenure, which is not captured in these data.

**PS8 (cultural heritage): triggered, medium.** A place of worship sits on the footprint edge, and a cemetery is about 2.9 km away. Wikidata lists Rufisque as a tentative World Heritage Site, about 2.9 km away. The Île de Gorée World Heritage site is about 11 km away and is unlikely to be affected directly. The OSM heritage layer is empty, but that reflects coverage, not absence. Chance-finds procedures will be needed.

**Category: provisionally B.** The asset is thermal, and the site is urban with sensitive receptors and a CR bird record. It would move to A if the capacity is large (IFC thresholds for thermal generation should be checked against the project's size and fuel) or if the impacts prove diverse or irreversible.

**Context.** The site lies in the Dakar coastal urban area of Senegal. No international or disputed boundary is within 15 km. Country-level governance, security and macroeconomic risk need external sources, which these tools do not provide.

**Gaps.** The data do not include: project capacity, fuel type, stack and cooling-water design, or footprint beyond the 0.5 km assumption; land tenure and any customary claims; groundwater, coastal flood and sea-level data; air-quality baselines; and the current state of the existing plants' environmental compliance. OSM coverage in Senegal is patchy, and the GBIF records are old in places.

**Desk research leads.** The Wikipedia pages returned are: Rufisque (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufisque), Kounoune power station (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kounoune_power_station) and Rufisque tramway (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufisque_tramway). I have not reviewed their content and they are undated here. The Rufisque heritage status should be checked against UNESCO's own list.
